descriptionChirho: To gird oneself around the waist, typically in preparation for service or action, fastening a garment or belt around the midsection. Used of servants keeping their waists girded in readiness (Luke 12:35), Jesus girding himself to serve the disciples (Luke 12:37; 17:8), the spiritual armor of truth girded around the waist (Eph 6:14), angels girded with golden sashes (Rev 15:6), and Christ girded with a golden sash across his chest (Rev 1:13). All multilingual glosses converge on girding/belting: Arabic mutanattiq/muntaqin, German umguertet, French ceindre, Hebrew chagar, Hindi kamar bandhna, Korean heori-e ttireul maeda, Spanish cenirse.
